chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar Al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Imam Ali (peace be upon him) did not see any problem if the person in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) were to wash his head in the early morning and wash the rest of his body at the time of prayer.

key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: The person in a state of major ritual impurity requiring full body wash
key_terms.غُدْوَةً: In the early morning / at dawn

ai.seo_question: Can a person wash their head and body separately during ghusl before prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence regarding the sequence of *ghusl al-janabah*, specifically validating the practice of washing the head in the morning and the rest of the body immediately before prayer. This ruling underscores the principle that the continuity of the wash (*muwalat*) is not strictly required for validity, provided the entire body is cleansed before the obligatory prayer time begins, reflecting the practical ease (*rukhsah*) granted to the faithful.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar Al Yamani, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said that:
‘Aliasws did not see any problem if the one with the sexual impurity were to wash his head early in the morning and washing the rest of his body during the Salaat’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar al-Yamaniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ‘Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would not consider it harmful if one washes his head earlier for Ghusl (bath) because of sexual relation and the rest of his body at the time of Salah (prayer).”’
